anxiety. Insomnia is a prominent complaint, followed by excitability and irritability. (from Ashton's manual)

questions.question_text:
A 19-year-old woman tells you that she takes MDMA. The least likely psychological consequence of this drug in short term (immediately after
use) is:

options.text: Increased desire to do mental tasks

questions.explanation:
MDMA can increase friendliness, empathising ability and increased the desire to be mentally active. It produces a relaxing calming e�ect and
not anxiety.

questions.question_text: The most common psychiatric presentation seen in those with cancer is
questions.explanation:
Prevalence of major depression in those with advanced cancer is about 5 –15%. About 10 –15% of cancer patients present with less severe
symptoms. The prevalence of depression in advanced disease is closer to 33% (Hotopf et al. 2001). Somatic symptoms are not useful when
diagnosing depression in the physically ill. Pervasive global anhedonia is a more valid criterion for the diagnosis of depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following signs is not present in Wernicke's encephalopathy?
questions.explanation:
Wernicke's encephalopathy (WE) is an acute condition characterized by the well-known triad of ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and global
confusional state. The classic triad of confusion, ataxia and nystagmus is only present in 10% of patients and 80% of patients are not
diagnosed before post mortem. These eye signs are usually bilateral but not necessarily symmetrical. WE is directly caused by acute
thiamine de�ciency, due to inadequate dietary intake, reduced gastrointestinal absorption, decreased hepatic storage and impaired
utilization. Peripheral neuropathy, a sign of beriberi, results from more chronic vitamin de�ciency states.

questions.question_text: The most common anxiety disorder according to National Psychiatric Morbidity Survey in UK is
questions.explanation:
15% of adults in UK at any time have broadly de�ned neurosis according to National Psychiatric Morbidity Survey. In NPMS 1995 UK
prevalence of anxiety disorder was higher than depression (consistent with ECA and NCS USA), Phobic disorder the most common in ECA
and NCS but in NPMS - the most common anxiety disorder was mixed anxiety-depression followed by GA 25% of all GP consultations are for
anxiety related symptoms.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of OCD in general population is;
questions.explanation: 2-3% in the general population (more in children than adults).

questions.question_text:
A 30-year-old man with clumsy gait, repeated falls and visual problems reports that his grandfather reportedly developed the same
condition and died at an age of 41 after myocardial infarction. The most likely diagnosis to be considered is
questions.explanation:
In Friedreich,s ataxia the spinal and peripheral nerves and cerebellum degenerate, a�ecting balance and movement and sensory functions
but with intact cognition. The disorder also causes problems in the heart and spine, and some people with the condition develop diabetes.
Various forms of heart disease often accompany Friedreich's ataxia, including hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, myocardial �brosis, and cardiac
failure. Heart block is also common. Heart disease is the most common cause of death. Friedreich's ataxia is an autosomal recessive,
trinucleotide expansion disease a�ecting GAA sequence of frataxin protein encoding gene on chromosome 9.

questions.question_text: Proportion of patients that do not respond to �rst trial of antidepressant is
questions.explanation:
30 to 45% of patients show no response to antidepressant treatment. Coexistent medical disorder, severe depression, alcohol use, familial
history of poor treatment response, etc. predispose to non-response

questions.question_text: What is the prevalence of clinical depression after stroke?
questions.explanation:
A meta-analysis, evaluating data from studies conducted between 1977 and 2002, estimated the prevalence of post-stroke depression at
33% (Hackett et al 2005b), even if with relevant di�erences across studies. The risk is elevated for a longer period of observation following
stroke.

questions.question_text: The standardised mortality ratio for patients with dysthymia is higher than the general population by a factor of
questions.explanation:
A meta-analytic study (Harris & Barraclough, 1997) found a standardized mortality ratio (SMR) for individuals diagnosed with dysthymia to be
12-fold higher compared to the general population. For major depression, the same study observed a 20=times higher SMR.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antidepressants is associated with minimal sexual dysfunction?
questions.explanation:
Agomelatine has probably the lowest risk of sexual dysfunction among currently available antidepressants in the UK. In the Phase 2/3 trials
Agomelatine had no adverse pro�le on orgasm, erection or libido. Incidence of sexual dysfunction was similar to placebo. (Ref: Seretti et al, J
Clin Psychopharmacology 2009; 29: 259-266)

questions.question_text:
Mrs. Y is treated for breast cancer with Tamoxifen. She is clinically depressed. Which of the following drugs is contraindicated in her
situation?
questions.explanation:
In several studies (notably, Jin et al, 2005), concurrent use of tamoxifen with the potent CYP2D6-inhibitor antidepressants paroxetine and
�uoxetine, was associated with a 65-75% reduction in circulating endoxifen (active metabolite of tamoxifen) levels in some women
(especially in poor metabolisers). Based on current research into psychotropics, the strongest CYP2D6 inhibitors are identi�ed as paroxetine,
�uoxetine, buproprion, duloxetine, while sertraline, escitalopram, and doxepin are moderate inhibitors, with venlafaxine being a weak
inhibitor. Therefore, if antidepressants are indicated in the treatment of a woman currently taking tamoxifen, avoid antidepressants such as
�uoxetine and paroxetine, bupropion and duloxetine. Co-administration with other potent CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g. quinidine, or bupropion)
should also be avoided whenever possible. (Retrieved from: Interactions Between Antidepressants and Tamoxifen: June 2008;
www.womensmentalhealth.org; June 2008)

questions.question_text:
You are talking to a nurse from the falls clinic. She wants to know the antipsychotic drug, which is least likely to cause orthostatic
hypotension. Which of the following would you recommend?
questions.explanation: Amisulpride produces minimal alpha adrenergic related e�ects and is unlikely to cause orthostatic hypotension.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antipsychotic drug is least likely to cause dry mouth and cognitive impairment?
questions.explanation: Amisulpride produces minimal anticholinergic side e�ects and is unlikely to cause dry mouth.

questions.question_text:
Rosy is a 20-year-old female who is concerned about her weight loss, diarrhoea and infrequent menstrual periods. She refuses to put the
central heating on in her �at because it makes her sweat a lot. Her father thinks she is trying to keep the nagging mother away. Her parents
are described as 'domineering,. What is her diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Although the symptoms mimic like an eating disorder, Rosy is experiencing classic symptoms of hyperthyroidism featured by weight loss,
diarrhoea, heat intolerance and infrequent menstrual periods.

questions.question_text: Proportion of patients with a major depressive episode that show an elevation in cortisol levels is
questions.explanation:
Around 50% of patients with major depressive disorder show cortisol elevation (around 40% in outpatients, and 60% of inpatients) when
compared to nondepressed individuals (Thase et al., 2002)

questions.question_text:
Mark has chronic pain and depression, which is not responding to SSRI antidepressants. Which one of the following is the best
antidepressant of choice in this situation?
questions.explanation:
As this patient has not responded to SSRIs, tricyclic antidepressants like Amitriptyline would be a good choice. Amitriptyline is also
prescribed frequently for the treatment of neuropathic pain.

questions.question_text: Which antibiotic can increase the plasma concentration of clozapine and should be avoided during clozapine therapy?
questions.explanation:
Avoid concomitant use of antibiotics that increase the risk of neutropenia whilst patient is on clozapine therapy. "This includes those that are
known to have a substantial potential to depress bone marrow function for example, sulphonamides, trimethoprim, co-trimoxazole and
nitrofurantoin, or those that increase the plasma concentration of clozapine such as erythromycin"(Clozapine A reminder about safe and
e�ective use. (n.d.). Retrieved from

A 21-year-old man spends most of his time in his room, browsing the Internet or playing computer-based games. He prefers online chats as
a form of socialisation but does not feel the need to socialise by making face-to-face contacts. He denies being depressed. He is likely to
have one of the following personality traits:
questions.explanation: Individuals with schizoid personality may prefer being on their own most of the time.

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors increase the risk of schizophrenia?
questions.explanation:
Being urban born increases the risk of schizophrenia two-fold compared to rural born individuals. Living in the city is also noted to increase
incidence of schizophrenia. The incidence of schizophrenia is 3 to 5 times more common in migrants than native population; this becomes
1.8 when considering prevalence rates. Winter/spring birth increases the risk of schizophrenia to a small extent (RR 1.11); but as prevalence
of birth itself is common in winter/spring, 10.5% of all schizophrenia incidences can be attributed to the seasonal birth. The winter/spring
excess is positively associated with latitude. Fluctuations in schizophrenia incidence have been reported over many decades.

questions.question_text: Which antipsychotic drug has a lower propensity for QTc prolongation?
questions.explanation:
Both Aripiprazole and Paliperidone appear to have lower propensity for QTc prolongation; with both of these drugs a notable QTc increase
has not been reported either at therapeutic doses or in overdose (as of yet).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS) is false?

options.text: Each item is rated in a 7 point scale
It is a clinician administered scale
Various versions of BPRS have 18 to 24 items
It can be used to assess e�ectiveness of treatment interventions
It measures symptoms of schizophrenia only

correct_answer.text: It measures symptoms of schizophrenia only

questions.explanation:
BPRS is a clinician-administered scale that measures various (18 or more) psychiatric symptoms in a Likert fashion. It was originally designed
to measure the e�cacy of interventions in psychotic disorders including schizophrenia, other psychoses, and depression, especially with
psychotic features.

questions.question_text:
A CT1 trainee is examining a patient for neurological signs & symptoms on the ward. Which feature is commonly seen in patients with
dominant parietal lobe dysfunction?
questions.explanation:
A speci�c syndrome, Gerstmann,s syndrome is associated with lesions of the dominant parietal lobe. This consists of dyscalculia, agraphia,
�nger agnosia and right-left disorientation. Anosognosia and dressing apraxia are often seen with non-dominant parietal lesions.

questions.question_text:
Mr P has been treated for non-psychotic depression with 40 mg of Paroxetine. There was a minimal response to this drug and augmentation
with another drug was suggested. The drug of choice in this scenario would be
questions.explanation:
One of the �rst choice treatments recommended for refractory depression is to combine SSRI with Mirtazapine or Mianserin. It is
recommended by NICE. It is usually well tolerated. There is reasonable literature support and is becoming more widely used. (Ref: The
Maudsley prescribing guidelines- 10th edition- page 179)

questions.question_text: Which of the following treatment is licensed to treat adult ADHD?
questions.explanation:
Atomoxetine can be used by teenagers and children over six. It is also licensed for use in adults who are continuing treatment after taking
the medication as a teenager. It is not licensed for use in adults newly diagnosed with ADHD. Methylphenidate and Dexamfetamine are not
licensed for use in adults.

questions.question_text: The main rationale to use melatonin in children with sleep disorders is to
questions.explanation:
Trials investigating melatonin use in children have demonstrated reduced sleep latency and increased sleep duration though the latter is
contested as melatonin is associated with earlier waking times. (BMJ 2012;345:e6664)

questions.question_text:
A 12-year-old boy with a history suggestive of depressive disorder had an adequate course of CBT but failed to show any treatment
response. His parents are not keen to start on medications. The best possible course of option is to prescribe
questions.explanation:
Family therapy is bene�cial for children who su�er from 'internalising' problems (for example, shyness, anxiety, depression, self esteem,
self-e�cacy) in children. (Ref: Woods et al., Research Report DFE-RR179 ww.gov.uk).

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is not a feature of oppositional de�ant disorder?
questions.explanation: Physical cruelty to animals is a feature seen in children with conduct disorder. All the other features are seen in children with ODD.

questions.question_text: What is the rate of completed suicide in the age range of 10-14?
questions.explanation:
The rates for male and females of completed suicide are 1-2 per 100000 in the age range of 10-14 years, 4-8 per 100000 in the age range of
15-19 years. 1% of school-age children reported a recent suicide attempt and 2% reported suicidal threats.(Ref: Oxford handbook of child
&adolescent psychiatry; Pg 268; Tishler et al., Suicidal Behavior in Children Younger than Twelve: A Diagnostic Challenge for Emergency
Department Personnel. Acad Emerg Med.2007 Sep;14(9):810-8)

questions.question_text: The proportion of all homicides perpetrated by individuals with schizophrenia is
questions.explanation:
Around 50 homicides per year are committed by those in recent contact with mental health services; this represents 9% of all homicides. 5%
of homicide perpetrators have a diagnosis of schizophrenia

questions.explanation:
Elderly sex o�enders and non-sex-o�enders have similar prevalence rates of mental illness (Fazel, 2006). However, elderly sex o�enders

questions.question_text: Victims of female homicide perpetrators with psychosis often belong to the age group of;
questions.explanation:
The victims of female homicide perpetrators are often in their own family. A substantial number of these victims are <16 years of age,
especially if the perpetrator has psychosis. 50% of mentally ill perpetrators of child homicide have a psychotic disorder. But note that fathers
are signi�cantly more likely to kill their children than mothers, if one considers all child homicides. Also 13% of perpetrators of �licide (child-
killing by parents) took their own life after killing their child (this is called �licide-suicide)

questions.question_text: Most o�enders with a charge of exhibitionism belong to the age groups
questions.explanation:
Most exhibitionists are male and their victims are usually female adults or children. Most males arrested for exhibitionism are in their late
teens or early twenties. In general, exhibitionists have the highest sex o�ense recidivism rates compared to other o�ender groups, though
recidivism reduces signi�cantly when charged/sentenced once.

questions.question_text: Among the members of Royal College of Psychiatrists, the percentage who experience stalking in any given time is
questions.explanation:
Nearly 22% psychiatrists considered themselves to have been stalked. Approximately 1 in 3 had experiences of stalking behaviours that met
the legal de�nition of harassment. On average, one College member became the victim of a new series of stalking behaviours every week
(51 new members per year).

questions.question_text: The proportion of those discharged from medium secure units that are convicted for a violent o�ence within 2 years of discharge is
questions.explanation:
Follow-up studies of Medium Secure discharges suggest that nearly 25% will be readmitted in the 12 months after discharge. The
reconviction rate for any o�ence in 2 years is 15%, but for violent o�ences this is 6%. This rate nearly doubles to 1 in 3 reo�ending in 5
years, but only 1 in 6 will be convicted for a violent o�ence. From high secure units, at least 20% of those discharged will never live in the
community in the ten years after discharge: they get re-institutionalised elsewhere. In this time, at least 15% would have been convicted for
a serious further o�ence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about paedophilia is incorrect?

options.text: 80% of o�enders are strangers unknown to the victims
The o�ender is usually a male
50-70% of paedophiles can be diagnosed as having another paraphilia
One third of the o�enders are adolescents
Girls are twice likely to be the victims

correct_answer.text: 80% of o�enders are strangers unknown to the victims

questions.explanation:
In paedophilia, 80% of o�enders against children are either relatives (13%) or are known to them (68%). The o�ender is usually a male (90%)
and commonly a relative. One-third of the o�enders are adolescents. Most victims are known to the o�ender and up to half are related.
Girls are twice likely to be the victims.

questions.question_text: Which of the following groups of sexual o�enders are more likely to be married than other sexual o�enders?
questions.explanation:
There is a commonly held stereotype for an exhibitionist to be a "dirty old man in a raincoat". But most males arrested for exhibitionism are
in their late teens or early twenties. About half of exhibitionists are married.

questions.question_text: A subcultural rather than neuropathological explantation for Learning disability is supported by which of the following?

options.text: Existence of profound degree of learning disability
Even distribution of LD across di�erent socioeconomic groups of the population

questions.explanation:
The following features are suggestive of a Subcultural LD rather than neuropathological explantation - Mild or borderline type, Mild or
borderline type, Family members may also have borderline IQ, Dysmorphic characters less likely, Syndromic features not seen, Behavioural
phenotypes rare

questions.question_text: HGPRT deletion mutation is linked to which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is related to a defect in hypoxanthine guanine phosphoribosyl-transferase (HGPRT) leading to an accumulation of
uric acid. This is an X-linked recessive condition leading to intellectual disability. Partial HGPRT de�ciency results in gout. Compulsive self-
mutilation is an important behavioural phenotype seen in this condition, which is very distressing to these children. Often severe self-biting

years. Men with this syndrome are reported to hit, spit, swear and even become aggressive towards their caregivers. Kidney failure
secondary to infection or uric acid deposition (urate stones) is the cause of death in most subjects.

questions.question_text: Which of the following genetic syndromes is known to have an association with the schizotypal disorder?
questions.explanation:
Individuals with Fragile X (23% of full mutants) and family members who carry the premutation may both show schizotypal features. The
presence of personality traits is not limited to schizotypal disorder: patients with fragile X also show schizoid traits and avoidant personality
traits.

questions.question_text: Lennox-Gastaut syndrome is characterized by

options.text: Triad of infantile spasms, spike-wave complex and mental retardation
Primarily caused by a metabolic encephalopathy

correct_answer.text: Triad of infantile spasms, spike-wave complex and mental retardation

questions.explanation:
Lennox-Gastaut syndrome is one of the most severe epileptic encephalopathies of childhood onset. It can occur secondary to an underlying
brain disorder or idiopathic (i.e., has no known cause). Although Lennox-Gastaut syndrome is commonly characterised by a triad of signs,
which include multiple seizure types, slow spike-wave complexes on EEG, and signi�cant learning disability. The children su�er frequent �ts
of many di�erent types, starting with infantile spasms that often evolve into full-blown syndrome; the age of onset is from 1 to 8 years,

(Excerpt retrieved from

options.text: Providing an insu�cient diagnostic explanation for genetically determined syndromes
Making more than one diagnosis for a behavioural problem
Making more than one diagnoses for a physical health problem
Attributing a psychiatric symptom to a behavioural phenotype
Attributing a health issue to an already existing health issue

Once a diagnosis is made of a major condition, there is a tendency to attribute all other problems to that diagnosis, thereby leaving other co-
existing conditions undiagnosed. In the context of learning disabilities this means that 'symptoms of physical ill health are mistakenly
attributed to either a mental health/behavioural problem or as being inherent in the person's learning disabilities' (Emerson and Baines,
2010). This issue is explicitly discussed in the GMC's guidelines regarding discrimination. See uk.org/learningdisabilities/200.aspx#207

questions.question_text: The one-year incidence of dementia in Parkinson's disease is;
questions.explanation:
The incidence of dementia in patients with Parkinson's disease is estimated to be around 10% every year. Mindham et al. found the number
of patients with dementia to be four times higher than expected over a period of 3 years.

A routine diagnostic workup shows high levels of calcium in an elderly patient. What other laboratory test needs to be done to interpret
these results?
questions.explanation:

the total serum calcium level. Directly measuring the free calcium level is more convenient and accurate, but a formula can also be used to
calculate the corrected total serum calcium level from plasma albumin concentrations. The causes of hypercalcemia usually can be
distinguished on the basis of measurement of serum phosphate and alkaline phosphatase. The thyroid-stimulating hormone can be
checked to help rule out hyperthyroidism.

questions.question_text:
An 81-year-old man with moderately severe dementia has been prescribed donepezil 10mg a day. Unfortunately, he develops signi�cant
gastrointestinal side e�ects. What is the most appropriate next step in action?
questions.explanation:
The GI side e�ects of antidementia drugs are known to occur less frequently at lower doses. So the �rst course of action is to drop the dose
to 5mg a day.

questions.question_text:
You are asked to assess a 75-year-old man with cognitive impairment in A&E. Which of the following would exclude an ICD-10 diagnosis of
dementia?

options.text: He is self-su�cient and functioning independently
Evidence of a decline in both memory and thinking
Change from previous level of functioning
The impairment has been noted for 12 months

correct_answer.text: He is self-su�cient and functioning independently

questions.explanation:
According to ICD-10 diagnostic guidelines, the primary requirement for diagnosis is evidence of a decline in both memory and thinking,
which is su�cient to impair personal activities of daily living. Evidence of clear consciousness is required. The impairments should have been
evident for at least six months for a con�dent clinical diagnosis of dementia to be made.

questions.question_text: What is the most appropriate investigation for a 65-year-old woman with progressive cognitive impairment?

options.text: Analysis of thyroid and thyroid-stimulating hormone levels

questions.explanation:
Progressive cognitive impairment is seen in people with senile dementia, probably of the Alzheimer's type. The most commonly employed
neuroimaging methods for identifying dementia are computerized tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). CT scan is useful
to identify di�use cerebral atrophy with enlargement of the cortical sulci and increased size of the ventricles. Disproportionate atrophy of
the medial temporal lobe, particularly of the volume of the hippocampal formations (< 50%), can be seen (Alzheimer Disease Imaging -

questions.question_text: Subcortical dementia is characterised by
questions.explanation:
Amnesia, aphasia, apraxia and normal executive function (during early stages) are features of cortical dementia. Impairment of attention &
executive function slowed up alertness, and apathetic personality are features of subcortical dementia.

questions.question_text: In an 83-year-old man with delirium, tremor & rigidity, which one of the following you would avoid?
questions.explanation:
This man has Parkinsonian symptoms. Antipsychotics must be avoided as it can worsen motor features of Parkinson's disease and can
exacerbate delirium or acute confusional state.

Acute confusional state (delirium) is common in older people, often precipitated by mechanical falls. The onset is acute, and the duration of
symptoms is very short. Transient paranoid delusions and hallucinations are commonly reported in delirium.
